first_signal: First consumer complaints received; Missouri Dept. of Agriculture then tested product
recall: Recall announced; expanded 2021-01-11 to all corn-containing products from the Oklahoma plant
source_label: FDA warning letter to Midwestern Pet Foods, Aug 2021

first_signal: Michigan Dept. of Agriculture found Salmonella in an unopened bag during routine retail testing
recall: Voluntary recall; expanded repeatedly through May 2012
harm: 49 human illnesses (47 in 20 states + 2 in Canada), 10 hospitalized (CDC)

first_signal: First poisoning case reported (Rochester, NY; Cornell AHDC)
recall: Recall of corn-containing products from the Gaston, SC plant
harm: 76 dog deaths, 21 ill reported to FDA CVM (Jan 2006); Cornell estimated 100+ deaths
source_label: Cornell Chronicle, Dec 2005; JAVMA news Feb 2006

episode: 2025 H5N1 in Wild Coast Raw chicken cat food
first_signal: Washington State Dept. of Agriculture public health alert naming the lots after cats fell ill (cat diagnoses were earlier and are undated)
harm: Multiple indoor cats in OR/WA infected, several euthanized

first_signal: Menu Foods' first complaints of sick pets and first problems in its taste-trial animals
recall: Recall of all 'cuts and gravy' products; grew to >5,300 products across many brands
harm: >17,000 complaints to FDA incl. ~1,950 cat and ~2,200 dog deaths reported (Apr 2007)
source_label: FDA CVM 2007 history; U.S. Senate hearing, Apr 2007

first_signal: Five dogs in one household fell acutely ill minutes after eating the food; one died
recall: Recall of Hunk of Beef lots; expanded Feb and Mar 2017
source_label: FDA warning letter to Evanger's, Jun 2017

episode: 2012 Diamond Salmonella, measured from first human illness onset
first_signal: Earliest human illness onset in the outbreak (only linked in hindsight)

episode: 2023 Mid America Pet Food (Victor) Salmonella Kiambu, measured from first human illness onset
first_signal: Earliest human illness onset (6 of 7 patients were infants); the recall itself followed a random South Carolina retail sample

episode: Chicken / duck / sweet-potato jerky treats made in China
first_signal: First FDA complaints ('since 2007'; secondary sources say August 2007)
recall: Market withdrawals (Waggin' Train, Canyon Creek Ranch, Milo's Kitchen) after NY State found unapproved antibiotic residues; not a formal recall and no cause proven
harm: >6,200 dogs, 26 cats, 3 people; >1,140 dog deaths reported (FDA, through 2015)
source_label: FDA CVM jerky treat investigation page
